text:
maria: Quick heads-up — hit a UX footgun in Go SDK generator: cancelling a streaming iter doesn't always release network FDs when retries kick in. small sampleapp repro included.

kevin: can you summarize repro steps?

maria: 1) run `./sampleapp gen --stream` against dev-runtime with 429/5xx injected
2) wait for first token, call cancel() or Ctrl-C
3) process lingers, sockets in CLOSE_WAIT, goroutines around streamer remain.

devon: that matches a flaky CI test we saw. sounds like retry/backoff timers ignore ctx.Done() and deferred closes live in goroutines that might not run.

jia: proposed fixes: (a) make retry/backoff select on ctx.Done() (do not use time.Sleep/time.After without ctx), (b) add Close() on GeneratorIter (idempotent) so callers can defer iter.Close(), (c) ensure ReadCloser wrapper returns EOF on ctx cancel so scanners exit.

kevin: prefer minimal API change — add Close() method and mark it safe to call multiple times. runtime changes should pass ctx into retry middleware. also add unit that asserts no goroutine leak.

maria: I'll open a small PR that: 1) adds GeneratorIter.Close(), 2) makes backoff ctx-aware, 3) updates sampleapp quickstart to defer Close(), and 4) includes a short troubleshooting blurb.

devon: include a regression integration test that simulates 429s then immediate cancel and listens for process exit within 500ms. that should catch future regressions.

jia: also grep for other time.After/time.Sleep uses in sdk and runtime and file follow-ups.

oncall-bot: reminder set — will ping #devex in 24h to check CI flakiness.

kevin: thanks — tag me for review on the runtime/backoff bit.

maria: will do. TL;DR: iterator Close + ctx-aware backoff + doc/test updates.
